C++ kernel for Jupyer Notebook (VS Code).

I tried following [creme's](https://creme332.github.io/posts/install-cpp-notebook/) blog, but I found it to be outdated. This install uses miniforge3 instead of mambaforge, as it's deprecated. The process for using the C++ kernel is also a little different.

To start, you will need the following:

- WSL (if using Windows)
- VS Code
- miniforge3

## Download the miniforge3 installer

On the [miniforge](https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge/releases) release page, download the file ending in 
'Linux-x86_64.sh' into the root directory of your terminal.

Then run the following command to install miniforge3:

```bash
sh ./Miniforge3-Linux-x86_64.sh
```

Replace 'Miniforge3-Linux-x86_64.sh' with your downloaded file. Press 'q' to skip the license and follow the rest of the instructions.

Reload your terminal and to verify the installation, run: 

```bash
mamba --version 
ls
```

You should see a folder called 'miniforge3' now.

## Install xeus-cling

xeus-cling (a Jupyter kernel for C/C++) isn't available on Windows (hence the reason WSL is needed), so in order to install it, run these three commands:

```bash
mamba create -n cling
source activate cling
mamba install xeus-cling -c conda-forge
```

If you want to install it from source, follow the instructions [here](https://github.com/jupyter-xeus/xeus-cling#installation-from-source)

**You can deactivate the environement by running:**

```bash
conda deactivate
```

## Install Jupyterlab

The last step is to install Jupyterlab via:

```bash
mamba install jupyterlab -c conda-forge
```

## C++ Kernel for VS Code 

Again, following creme's instructions, install the following extensions:

* Jupyter by Microsoft
* Jupyter Keymap by Microsoft
* Jupyter Cell Tags by Microsoft
* Jupyter Notebook Renderers by Microsoft

Following his instructions for the environment didn't work for me, so I had to work around it. First, create a file with the ipynb extension and with the cling environment active, run:

```bash
jupyter server password
```

Enter your password twice, then after it has been hashed, run:

```bash
jupyter lab 
```

Your server should come online, but look for the 'localhost' url. Copy that to your clipboard and in VS Code, click on 'select kernel'.

I didn't see a C++ kernel, and if you don't, click 'select another kernel' and then click 'existing jupyter server'. Paste in your link and enter your password. You now have the C++ kernel!

If you found any problems, please let me know, but I hope this is helpful for anyone trying to create C/C++ notebooks in VS Code.
